pending_commit.commit_message: CHROMIUM: driver-core: add test module for async firmware load There are some use-after-free bugs in the firmware-request framework. Pull this test module from Luis R. Rodriguez to test for this. Code from: https://github.com/mcgrof/fake-firmware-test/tree/next-20150505-fix-use-after-free or particularly: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mcgrof/fake-firmware-test/next-20150505-fix-use-after-free/test.c Quoting Luis: With a fixed kernel you should see: [ 283.512445] firmware name: test_module_stuff.bin [ 287.514020] firmware name: test_module_stuff.bin [ 287.532489] firmware found With a buggy kernel you should see a request for arbitrary files but in the most common case you kernel will crash due to a page fault on trying to free something you cannot and/or NULL pointer dereference. [NOTE: some of the above kernel messages only appear if we apply another patch to the kernel, to help reproduce the bug more easily. We have not applied that patch.] So far, I've seen crashes from loading this module. Crashes are not guaranteed reproducible (it's a race). BUG=chromium:557355 TEST=put anytything at /lib/firmware/test_module_stuff.bin; build and load module Change-Id: Ie3e6191049948b6348dacd37a161fb17398c9799 Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/313155 Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: driver-core: fixup modprobe status reporting for async firmware test While this module can uncover bugs in some cases, it is insufficient in two aspects: (1) It doesn't print a clear message to the log; if we manage to hit the "not found" case, it will confusingly print both "No firmware found" and "firmware found". Let's print only one of those messages. (2) There are other symptoms of failure, even if we don't see a page fault / NULL dereference; for instance, the firmware core might see a junk or empty string for the file name, and fail to load the firmware. This is also a symptom of use-after-free. For problem #2, it makes sense to actually wait for the async request to complete, and verify the load status. If the firmware failed to load, then the module init routine can report an error. If the firmware loaded successfully, then we report success. Note that a "success" still doesn't necessarily mean we have no use-after-free bug; it could just mean that the firmware loader won the race. BUG=chromium:557355 TEST=build and load module Change-Id: I5fba7e3d091dbe6ab7ddd51dcf04256833fa110f Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/313156 Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: Fix firmware loader uevent buffer NULL pointer dereference The firmware class uevent function accessed the "fw_priv->buf" buffer without the proper locking and testing for NULL. This is an old bug (looks like it goes back to 2012 and commit 1244691c73b2: "firmware loader: introduce firmware_buf"), but for some reason it's triggering only now in 4.2-rc1. Shuah Khan is trying to bisect what it is that causes this to trigger more easily, but in the meantime let's just fix the bug since others are hitting it too (at least Ingo reports having seen it as well). Reported-and-tested-by: Shuah Khan <shuahkh@osg.samsung.com> Acked-by: Ming Lei <ming.lei@canonical.com> Cc: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org> Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org> (cherry picked from commit 6f957724b94cb19f5c1c97efd01dd4df8ced323c) BUG=chromium:557355 TEST=build and boot Change-Id: I1328b4748069660a26d6c3bd5a332c57299f9316 Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/313200 Reviewed-by: Kees Cook <keescook@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: firmware: fix possible use after free on name on asynchronous request Asynchronous firmware loading copies the pointer to the name passed as an argument only to be scheduled later and used. This behaviour works well for synchronous calling but in asynchronous mode there's a chance the caller could immediately free the passed string after making the asynchronous call. This could trigger a use after free having the kernel look on disk for arbitrary file names. In order to force-test the issue you can use a test-driver designed to illustrate this issue on github [0], use the next-20150505-fix-use-after-free branch. With this patch applied you get: [ 283.512445] firmware name: test_module_stuff.bin [ 287.514020] firmware name: test_module_stuff.bin [ 287.532489] firmware found Without this patch applied you can end up with something such as: [ 135.624216] firmware name: \xffffff80BJ [ 135.624249] platform fake-dev.0: Direct firmware load for \xffffff80Bi failed with error -2 [ 135.624252] No firmware found [ 135.624252] firmware found Unfortunatley in the worst and most common case however you can typically crash your system with a page fault by trying to free something which you cannot, and/or a NULL pointer dereference [1]. The fix and issue using schedule_work() for asynchronous runs is generalized in the following SmPL grammar patch, when applied to next-20150505 only the firmware_class code is affected. This grammar patch can and should further be generalized to vet for for other kernel asynchronous mechanisms. @ calls_schedule_work @ type T; T *priv_work; identifier func, work_func; identifier work; identifier priv_name, name; expression gfp; @@ func(..., const char *name, ...) { ... priv_work = kzalloc(sizeof(T), gfp); ... - priv_work->priv_name = name; + priv_work->priv_name = kstrdup_const(name, gfp); ... (... when any if (...) { ... + kfree_const(priv_work->priv_name); kfree(priv_work); ... } ) ... when any INIT_WORK(&priv_work->work, work_func); ... schedule_work(&priv_work->work); ... } @ the_work_func depends on calls_schedule_work @ type calls_schedule_work.T; T *priv_work; identifier calls_schedule_work.work_func; identifier calls_schedule_work.priv_name; identifier calls_schedule_work.work; identifier some_work; @@ work_func(...) { ... priv_work = container_of(some_work, T, work); ... + kfree_const(priv_work->priv_name); kfree(priv_work); ... } [0] motion: wake up main task for all changes in EC parameter. We need to wake up the main task, even if we disable a sensor. It will force sending the sensors samples in the FIFO and put a timestamp behind them. Also, reduce the interrupt period by 10us to be sure we fire interrupt to the AP even if there are some variation in the timing calculation. BUG=b:24367625 BRANCH=smaug TEST=Run ts.SingleSensorTests overnight. Change-Id: I6d966d52b5cbb72ba5eb936bc2fad6c06c7d8605 Signed-off-by: Gwendal Grignou <gwendal@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/312986 Reviewed-by: Alec Berg <alecaberg@chromium.org>

motion: improve readability by adding units to variable names. Throughout the code, there are comparison between frequency (in mHz) and period (in us). CHROMIUM: usb: gadget: Fix handling of unrecognized OS descriptor requests If composite_setup() receives a control request for an OS Feature Descriptor that is not Extended Compatibility ID or Extended Properties, it falls through to enqueueing a response of length 'value' bytes which, because the request is not recognized, is -EOPNOTSUPP. Fix it so that we instead bail out of composite_setup() without enqueueing a response. The UDC driver is then responsible for halting EP0. BUG=chrome-os-partner:47809 TEST=Build and boot on Smaug. glados: Make SLP_S0 a non-interrupt input pin SLP_S0 can reside at an intermediate voltage even with the internal pull-down. Eliminate interrupt storms by making this pin a non-interrupt, which also necessitates making the pin a non-power signal. This change will inhibit us from enabling S0ix later on glados.
